clue.text: Tom tells Bob to change into naval dress

indicators.note: the names Tom, tells and Bob are told to change into something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One sailor instructs another to put on his uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change into' signals rearranging all the letters of TOM TELLS BOB. Flared trousers were the traditional uniform of naval ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: Flared sailors' trousers are the classic garment of the navy's ratings.

clue.text: Admit Bonn is playing a game

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of Admit Bonn fooling about and taking a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that the German city of Bonn is taking part in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals rearranging ADMIT BONN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Things for baby not ready — still coming in

indicators.note: coming in tells us one word enters the middle of the other

parts.note: something not ready on time is late
still, as in 'not yet', means yet

explanation.surface: The baby's things haven't arrived, and more are still on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'motionless', but here it means 'up to now'; 'coming in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the full set of clothes and bedding gathered for a newborn.

clue.text: Ship's officer has chair for one working on the side

definitions.text: chair for one working on the side

explanation.surface: A naval officer is given a seat to use while working over the ship's side.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: a bosun's chair is the plank seat slung on ropes for a sailor working on the hull, so the officer's title names the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosun is the petty officer in charge of rigging and deck crew; the bosun's chair, a slung seat, carries the title.

clue.text: Having got drunk fast

explanation.surface: Someone who has been drinking quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast here means firmly fixed, as in 'hold fast', not quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for inebriated, and also secure or firmly fixed, like a knot that will not slip.

clue.text: French city offering alternative to unproductive south

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
lean years are unproductive ones

explanation.surface: A French town is held up as a better option than the barren southern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Loire is famous for Joan of Arc's relief of its siege.

clue.text: Dress for period at work

explanation.surface: Choosing what to wear for a stint on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: A shift is a loose straight dress as well as a spell of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple straight-cut frock, and also a stint of hours worked by a team in rotation.

clue.text: Ill? Very much

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are sick replies emphatically.
explanation.definitionFit: Poorly, as in 'did poorly', and greatly, as in 'want something greatly'.

clue.text: It may make unconscious improvement in one's looks

definitions.text: It may make unconscious improvement in one's looks

parts.words: It may make unconscious improvement in one's looks
parts.note: reads like a cosmetic treatment, but the unconscious state is simply being asleep early in the night, said to refresh the face

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment that works without your noticing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names sleep before midnight, jokingly credited with keeping a person attractive.

clue.text: Shark will tear flesh with gain

indicators.note: tear suggests ripping the words flesh and gain apart and reassembling the pieces

explanation.surface: A predatory shark rips into meat for profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will tear' signals rearranging FLESH and GAIN together. The angel shark is also called the angelfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The angel shark, a flattened bottom-dwelling species, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Stirring things up here risks a stinging response

definitions.text: Stirring things up here risks a stinging response

parts.words: Stirring things up here risks a stinging response
parts.note: taken literally, poking a wasp-like insects' home gets you stung; figuratively, it is a place of angry trouble

explanation.surface: A warning that provocation invites a sharp retort.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation full of angry trouble, from disturbing a colony of large wasps.

clue.text: In Belgravia, tests reveal flies

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of letters Belgravia, tests

explanation.surface: Laboratory trials in a smart London district uncover insects.
explanation.walkthrough: BELGRAVIA is an upmarket district of London. 'flies' looks like the insects but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot an aircraft is to take to the air, the sense of the verb flies.

clue.text: Judas's characteristic, to take gold

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A remark on what typified Judas: grabbing the money.
explanation.walkthrough: Judas betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot is the archetypal betrayer, so his name stands for any turncoat.

clue.text: Handle: let it turn

indicators.note: turn suggests the letters of let it turning round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave a door handle to rotate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' signals rearranging LET IT; a plain reversal would give TITEL, so it is an anagram. Handle is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is informal for a name or designation, such as a nobleman's rank.

clue.text: A right pair of road hazards brings an end to aggressiveness

parts.note: fog is a danger to drivers
a frozen surface is another danger to drivers

explanation.surface: Two dangers on the road somehow cure a driver's road rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pair of' tells you 'road hazards' gives two pieces, MIST and ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreed cessation of fighting between warring sides.

clue.text: Men assert wrongly this apparent discovery is worthless

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters of Men assert are in the wrong order and must be sorted

explanation.surface: Some men claim mistakenly that a find has no value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' signals rearranging MEN ASSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an illusory find, something thought remarkable that proves a hoax or delusion.

clue.text: Press is to introduce French article

parts.note: to import is to bring in or introduce
une is the feminine indefinite article in French

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about bringing in a French piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is a verb: to urge persistently.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester is to press someone repeatedly with demands.

clue.text: Miserably nursed own drink

indicators.note: miserably suggests the letters of nursed own are in a sorry, jumbled state

explanation.surface: A gloomy person nurses a drink alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miserably' signals rearranging NURSED OWN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an evening cocktail taken at sunset.

clue.text: No limit to speech

parts.note: O, the figure nought, stands for no or nothing
a ration is a fixed limit on an allowance

explanation.surface: A declaration that speech should be unrestricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No limit' reads as unlimited, but it is two pieces: O and RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal address delivered on a ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: Looks with astonishment at first of great primates

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of great is used

parts.note: apes are primates

explanation.surface: Visitors at the zoo stare in wonder at the big apes.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed in amazement.

clue.text: Sweet Miss Brown's state

explanation.surface: A question about where a charming lady named Brown lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet Georgia Brown' is a jazz standard of 1925, also the Harlem Globetrotters' theme tune.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the lady in a famous jazz song, and a southern US state (or a Caucasus nation).

clue.text: Take me back-I think highly of Arab country

indicators.note: take me back means the word me is read backwards

parts.note: to rate someone is to think highly of them

explanation.surface: A lover pleads to be taken back, saying how much they admire their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf.

clue.text: One's given a bill for child due to go under the knife

definitions.text: child due to go under the knife

parts.note: one is I, and 's adds S
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A child heading for surgery is presented with the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Abraham was told to sacrifice his son, and raised the knife before an angel stopped him.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son was bound on the altar to be sacrificed before an angel intervened.

clue.text: Initially encourage to undertake difficult exercise for pianist

definitions.text: Initially encourage to undertake difficult exercise for pianist

indicators.note: Initially means the first letter of each of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Advice to push a pianist into a hard practice piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'encourage to undertake difficult exercise' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A study composed to develop a pianist's technique.

clue.text: Whip the company into a spurt

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a surge is a sudden spurt

explanation.surface: A coach urges the team on with a whip for a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash used for flogging, the noun sense of the clue word.

clue.text: Piano has wide range — not an original observation

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
latitude is freedom or wide scope

explanation.surface: Praise for a piano's broad compass, dismissed as a cliche.
explanation.definitionFit: A trite, hackneyed remark repeated so often it says nothing new.

clue.text: Sound from pig at last — the tiniest one

indicators.note: at last means only the closing letter of pig is used

parts.note: the runt is the smallest animal of a litter

explanation.surface: A piglet, smallest of the litter, finally makes a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound from pig' looks like the definition, but 'pig' is needed for its last letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A low guttural noise, the kind a hog makes.

clue.text: Give full attention to what may need solution

explanation.surface: Advice to focus hard on finding the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a liquid concentrate, which must be diluted in a solution; the surface pretends 'solution' means solving a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: To focus the mind, and a condensed liquid such as squash that needs diluting with water.
